eventMetadata.context_description: **Trader consensus centers on 33°C as the most probable daily maximum for Panama City on August 9, reflecting the interplay of seasonal climatology and current synoptic conditions.** In Panama’s tropical wet season, the Intertropical Convergence Zone typically brings persistent cloud cover, high humidity, and frequent showers that cap afternoon heating near the long-term August average of 30–32 °C. Recent forecast guidance from regional models indicates limited rainfall and slightly reduced cloudiness today, allowing surface temperatures to reach or briefly exceed 33 °C before convective activity develops. The 14 % probability assigned to 34 °C captures the tail risk of stronger insolation or delayed convection, while lower outcomes remain unlikely given the absence of anomalous cooling influences. Market-implied odds therefore embed the narrow but physically plausible range shaped by the latest observational trends and ensemble spread.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Wellington’s early August climatology centers on daily highs near 12–14°C, with modest day-to-day variability driven by passing fronts and southerly airflow.** Current short-range model guidance and official outlooks for 10 August 2026 converge on a maximum near 14–15°C under partly cloudy to clearing conditions, consistent with the market’s heaviest weighting on those two outcomes (46.5 % and 31.5 %). Recent days have run slightly cooler—10 °C on 6 August and 11 °C on 1 August—reflecting a transient cool spell that has since eased, allowing the 13 °C bucket (19.5 %) to remain viable if a front lingers or cloud cover suppresses insolation.

NIWA’s seasonal outlook for central New Zealand places August temperatures at near-average probabilities, providing no strong signal for either anomalous warmth or prolonged cold. Resolution hinges on the official MetService or equivalent verified maximum at Wellington’s reference station; traders therefore price the narrow 13–15 °C window most heavily because ensemble guidance shows limited upside beyond 16 °C and negligible downside below 12 °C for this specific date. No major synoptic shifts or data revisions have emerged in the past 48 hours to alter that consensus.

This market will resolve based on the highest temperature recorded in the 'Daily Observations' table on Weather Underground, not the figure displayed in the 'Day High & Low' summary section; in the event of any discrepancy between the two, the Daily Observations table shall be the primary resolution source not the Day High & Low section.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Shenzhen Bao'an International Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 10 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Shenzhen Bao'an International Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/cn/shenzhen/ZGSZ.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

This market will resolve based on the highest temperature recorded in the 'Daily Observations' table on Weather Underground, not the figure displayed in the 'Day High & Low' summary section; in the event of any discrepancy between the two, the Daily Observations table shall be the primary resolution source not the Day High & Low section.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Sao Paulo-Guarulhos International Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/br/guarulhos/SBGR.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Forecast models from Brazil’s National Institute of Meteorology (INMET) and major numerical weather prediction ensembles currently converge on a daytime maximum of 17–18°C for São Paulo on August 10, driven by persistent cloud cover, south-easterly flow, and the absence of strong subtropical high-pressure ridging that normally supports seasonal highs near 23–25°C. Recent runs show slightly cooler guidance than earlier in the week, reflecting increased moisture and reduced insolation that has lowered trader-implied probabilities for outcomes above 19°C while concentrating volume around 17–18°C. These temperatures align with observed cooling trends over the prior 48 hours and sit below August climatological averages, though minor model spread in boundary-layer mixing and timing of any weak frontal passage keeps a narrow window for 19°C still viable. Updated INMET briefings and 12–18-hour forecast revisions expected overnight remain the key near-term catalysts.

eventMetadata.context_description: Traders see near-equal implied odds for 70-71°F and 72-73°F highs in San Francisco on August 10 because official National Weather Service model guidance shows a narrow range centered near 71-72°F amid typical late-summer marine-layer variability. Onshore flow and a modest Pacific high-pressure ridge are expected to limit inland heating while allowing partial afternoon clearing, with wind speeds and the precise depth of the cool, moist marine layer serving as the key variables that differentiate the two leading bins. Historical climatology places August daily maxima around 69-70°F at downtown stations, so any slight delay in fog burn-off or stronger sea breeze could cap readings at the lower end, whereas reduced cloud cover would push toward the mid-70s. New model runs and updated NWS forecasts through the evening of August 9 remain the next data points likely to shift positioning.

eventMetadata.context_description: Forecast models and Mexico City's climatological baseline position 24–25°C as the leading outcomes for the August 10 daily high, with the market assigning combined implied probability above 70%. At 2,240 m elevation, afternoon convective clouds and showers typical of the peak rainy season limit insolation and cap temperatures near the long-term August mean of 24°C. Recent AccuWeather guidance shows daily highs ranging 22.8–25.5°C through the month with no anomalous warming signals, while ensemble guidance maintains similar values for the immediate forecast window. Minor upside risk to 26°C exists if drier conditions develop, but current moisture patterns favor the central cluster around 24°C.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Marcos A. Gelabert Intl Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 10 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Marcos A. Gelabert Intl Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/pa/panama-city/MPMG.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Trader sentiment for Panama City's August 10 peak temperature centers on short-term model guidance indicating highs near or slightly above the seasonal 29–32°C baseline amid the rainy season's high humidity and frequent convection. The 34°C outcome leads at 33.5% implied probability because recent ensemble runs favor modest warming from reduced cloud cover and light winds, while 35°C and 33°C capture forecast spread from variable thunderstorm timing and Atlantic moisture influx. Key variables include urban heat-island effects at the measurement site, trade-wind strength modulating boundary-layer mixing, sea-surface temperatures sustaining instability, and potential tropical wave passages that could enhance rainfall and cap daytime maxima. High uncertainty stems from typical model divergence on convective initiation within 24–48 hours, with NOAA and local meteorological updates expected to refine resolution criteria before the close.
